content: {"rule":"K-G4","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text uses Matthew 1:18 and Matthew 1:25 to break C3's link, which the rule governs as a verse used to break a link counted as an unanswered witness.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D2 vs C3 (Matthew 1:18, 25): CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN -- [L1] Matthew 1:18 \"before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost\" and Matthew 1:25 \"knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son\" contradict C3's claim of espousal union;","rule_words":"A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge uses to break a link is counted this way.","room":"'only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round' — one reading requires an actual quotation plus the round name before the verse can count; the other would allow bare citation or assertion without quotation/naming.","why":"The judge breaks C3's link using Matthew 1:18 and Matthew 1:25 but neither quotes an earlier-round sentence pressing those verses against that link nor names the round, so the rule's required condition is not met."}
